- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; apply downward bias to subsequent forecast steps.
- Model frequently overestimates in 1–3 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for short-term forecasts.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to adjust; increase downward bias in forecast if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% in next 2–3 steps.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate when sentiment is high and recent price is volatile; apply 2–5% downward correction if sentiment > 0.67 and price volatility > 2% over last 5 days.
